15-060.r: NALSA (Legal Services Authorities Act 1987): free, competent legal services to weaker sections on equal opportunity; organises Lok Adalats; guides State legal services authorities.

15-061.r: Free legal aid (Section 12, Legal Services Authorities Act): SC/ST, trafficking victims, women, children, disabled, industrial workmen, low-income persons; not all OBCs or all senior citizens.
15-061.t: Senior citizens get free aid only within State income ceilings (Delhi: 2 lakh), not automatically.

15-062.r: Right to Information is a legal right (RTI Act 2005), not a DPSP. DPSPs: equal pay (39(d)), adequate livelihood (39(a)), prohibition of liquor, right to work.

15-063.r: Uniform Civil Code → DPSP, Article 44 (State shall endeavour to secure it throughout India). Press freedom, religious freedom, equality before law are Fundamental Rights.

15-064.r: Only prohibition of liquor is a DPSP (Article 47). Bans on child labour in factories, begar or forced labour, and untouchability are Fundamental Rights.

15-066.r: K.T. Shah: Directive Principles are 'a cheque payable at the bank's convenience'.
15-066.h: Shah sounds like 'Sahukar' (moneylender): the cheque remark is his.

15-067.r: National Social Assistance Programme (15 August 1995) → fulfils DPSP on right to work, education, public assistance; includes old age pension, family benefit, maternity benefit schemes.

15-068.r: In Part IV: equal pay for equal work (39(d)), Uniform Civil Code (44). Not DPSP: small family norm; mother-tongue primary education → Article 350A.

16-001.r: Fundamental Duties (Article 51-A, Part IV-A; 42nd Amendment 1976, Swaran Singh Committee) are non-justiciable: no legal process to enforce them; not correlative to legal duties.

16-002.r: Fundamental Duties → Part IV-A, Article 51A, added by 42nd Amendment 1976 on Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation; originally 10, now 11.
16-002.h: Swaran = gold: Swaran Singh gave the golden duties.

16-004.r: Swaran Singh Committee recommended (1976) Fundamental Duties → 42nd Amendment Act 1976 inserted Article 51A (Part IV-A), in force 3 January 1977; 11th duty (k) added later.

16-006.r: Article 51A(c), the third duty → uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India. Duties came via the 42nd Amendment.

16-008.r: 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Article 51A in new Part IV-A → Fundamental Duties of citizens.

16-013.r: Swaran Singh Committee (1976): 12 members incl. A.R. Antulay, S.S. Ray, C.M. Stephen; Haridev Joshi (Rajasthan CM) was not a member. 42nd Amendment added ten duties.

16-021.r: Fundamental Duties cannot be enforced by writs; they are moral obligations (patriotism, unity of India), promoted by constitutional methods and usable to interpret ambiguous statutes.

16-022.r: Voting in elections is not a Fundamental Duty; Article 51A has 11 duties incl. scientific temper, safeguarding public property, abiding by the Constitution.

16-024.r: Article 51A(a) → abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem.

16-025.r: Value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture → Fundamental Duty, Article 51A(f); separation of judiciary, free education, abolition of untouchability are not duties.

16-026.r: Striving to abolish untouchability is not a Fundamental Duty; untouchability is dealt with by Article 17, a Fundamental Right (Part III).

16-027.r: Organising village panchayats is a DPSP (Article 40), not a Fundamental Duty. Duties: defend country and render national service (51-A(d)), composite culture, public property, abjure violence.

16-029.r: Fundamental Duties include preserving composite culture, scientific temper and inquiry, striving towards excellence; 'protect weaker sections from social injustice' is not a duty.

16-030.r: Article 51A(g) → protect and improve natural environment incl. forests, lakes, rivers, wildlife; compassion for living creatures. 51A(a) → respect the National Flag.
16-030.t: The duty is to respect the National Flag, not 'protect' it; protection of wildlife is the duty asked.

16-031.r: Citizen's duty to protect and improve the natural environment → Article 51A(g), Part IV-A. (Article 48-A is the State's DPSP on environment.)

16-032.r: Fundamental Duties are not part of Fundamental Rights; they form Part IV-A (Article 51A), added by 42nd Amendment 1976; now 11 duties.

16-033.r: Protecting monuments and places of public importance is not in Article 51A; duties include respecting the National Anthem, safeguarding public property, protecting environment.

16-034.r: Protecting monuments and places of national importance → DPSP, Article 49, not a Fundamental Duty.
16-034.t: Don't confuse 'safeguard public property' (duty) with 'protect monuments' (DPSP, Article 49).

16-035.r: Respecting parents and teachers is not among the eleven Fundamental Duties; respecting the National Flag, brotherhood and composite culture are.

16-036.r: Voting in public elections is not a Fundamental Duty. Scientific temper → 51A(h); safeguard public property → 51A(i); abide by Constitution → 51A(a).

16-037.r: Wrong pair: Fundamental Duties → Part IV-A (42nd Amendment), not Part V; Part V = Union Executive. Part II Citizenship, III Fundamental Rights, IV DPSP.

16-038.r: All three correct: separation of judiciary → DPSP (Article 50); preserving composite culture → Fundamental Duty (51A(f)); child employment ban → Fundamental Right (Article 24).

16-039.r: Uphold and protect sovereignty, unity and integrity of India → Fundamental Duty, Article 51A(c). Duties added by 42nd and 86th Amendments; now 11.

16-040.r: Eleven Fundamental Duties; originally 10; 11th (51A(k): parents/guardians give education opportunity to children aged 6 to 14) added by 86th Amendment Act 2002.

16-041.r: Respect for international law → Article 51(c) (DPSP); compassion for living creatures → 51A(g); spirit of inquiry and reform → 51A(h); separate judiciary → Article 50.
16-041.t: Article 51 (DPSP) and Article 51A (Duties) differ by one letter; don't mix them.

17-001.r: Head of the Indian Republic (Head of State) → President of India; first President Dr. Rajendra Prasad (26 Jan 1950 to 13 May 1962).

17-003.r: A true, R false: India's President is indirectly elected, unlike the hereditary British King; but not similar to the US President, who has more power.

17-004.r: Article 53 → Union executive power vested in the President (A true); R false: he acts directly or through subordinate officers as per the Constitution, so his power is limited.

17-005.r: Article 53(1) → President exercises Union executive power directly or through officers subordinate to him, per the Constitution. Article 52 → there shall be a President.

17-006.r: Executive Head of State → President; Article 53 vests the executive power of the Union in the President.

17-011.r: Both true, R explains A: Article 53 vests Union executive power in the President, who is the constitutional head of the State.

17-012.r: Both true, R does not explain A: Article 53 vests executive power in the President; Article 77 → all executive action of Government of India taken in the President's name.

17-013.r: Article 53(2) → supreme command of the Defence Forces vested in the President, but its exercise is regulated by law (not free of legislative control).

17-014.r: 'Represents the nation but does not lead it' → President (Head of State); the Prime Minister holds real executive power and leads the nation.

17-015.r: President elected indirectly (Article 54) by an electoral college, through proportional representation by single transferable vote, by secret ballot.

17-027.r: Presidential election cannot be postponed because the electoral college is incomplete (e.g. a dissolved Assembly). Term five years; incumbent continues till successor enters office.

17-028.r: Presidential nomination needs at least 50 electors as proposers and another 50 as seconders.
17-028.c: No answer printed: the correct figure, 50, is not among the options.

17-029.r: MLA vote value = State population ÷ elected MLAs ÷ one thousand (not ×100); MP vote value = total value of all MLAs' votes ÷ total elected MPs (Article 55).

17-030.r: MLA vote value varies by State (Arunachal Pradesh 8, Uttar Pradesh 208); every MP of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha has the same vote value.

17-031.r: Incorrect: MLA votes = multiples of one thousand, not one hundred. Correct: 1971 census basis till first census after 2026 (84th Amendment 2001); PR by single transferable vote.

17-032.r: 2022 Presidential election: Rajasthan MLA vote value = 129 (1971 population 2,57,65,800 ÷ 200 MLAs ÷ 1000 = 128.82). Droupadi Murmu became 15th President.

17-033.r: Only one correct: nominated members excluded from electoral college; more Assembly seats → lower MLA vote value; values: Madhya Pradesh 131, Kerala 152, Arunachal 8, Puducherry 16.
